metadata.title: Review, Not Repair.
metadata.subtitle: The Accessibility Review Skill
metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Plain register: when you ask Claude to review a design for accessibility, does it fix the design, or check it against a standard? Lands the carry-out that accessibility-review is an audit, not a repair — it checks a design against WCAG 2.1 AA and reports where it fails, the same way every time.

beats.narration_text: Someone assumed accessibility review means Claude fixes the design. It doesn't — it checks the design against a fixed standard. So: how do I get Claude to review my design for accessibility?

beats.narration_text: A skill is a folder Claude reads before it works. This one is accessibility-review — a single SKILL.md file, about four kilobytes. It's the whole instruction set, written in plain language, with no hidden logic underneath it. Claude reads it, then acts on what it says. The file is the program.

Its job, word for word: run a WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility audit on a design or page. It triggers on requests like auditing accessibility, checking a11y, or asking if a design is accessible — or before handing off work that touches color contrast, keyboard navigation, touch target size, or screen reader behavior. Once triggered, Claude reads the Steps section and runs them in order — linear, no branching unless a step says so.

production_viz.label: HOW IT GETS PICKED UP
production_viz.caption: only runs when the words match

beats.narration_text: That's an audit, not a repair. The skill checks a design against a fixed standard, WCAG 2.1 AA, and reports exactly where it fails — it doesn't rewrite the design to fix what it finds. Run the same design through twice, and the audit comes back the same both times. But it only checks what that standard covers — anything outside WCAG 2.1 AA is outside what this skill sees.

production_viz.label: AN AUDIT, NOT A REPAIR
production_viz.caption: it reports gaps, it doesn't close them

beats.narration_text: accessibility-review doesn't fix a design — it checks it against WCAG 2.1 AA and reports exactly where it fails, the same way every time.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude: I want to audit a design for accessibility — read the accessibility-review skill and walk me through what you will do before you do it. That clause matters: having Claude explain itself first, before it acts, is how you actually see the instructions it's following, not just the result.
